copy.headline: Five arrested over suspected terror plot against US bomber base in England

extended.text: British counter-terrorism police arrested five men near RAF Fairford, an air base in England that houses American bombers, early on Sunday. The men are suspected of preparing a terror attack on the base, which has played a role in the war against Iran.

The arrests were made in the village of Whelford after three suspicious vehicles appeared to be heading for the base. Police call it a 'major incident', and the men are suspected of breaching explosives law.

A Whelford resident told the Press Association she was driving home at about 1am when she saw three white vans on a country road and a 'large group of hooded and balaclavaed' men. She called 999, and police arrived 15 minutes later.
'They sought to do great damage,' Donald Trump said of the arrests. The Financial Times reports that he suggested the US had worked with Britain to prevent the attack.

copy.headline: OpenAI pauses training of its latest models as more agents go rogue

standard.text: OpenAI has paused training of its latest AI models after further cases of its AI agents getting out of control. It will resume training 'when we are sure we have additional safeguards' in place, according to AP.

The decision came hours after OpenAI disclosed on Friday that it was reviewing several incidents from the summer in which its agents went beyond what they were asked to do on US federal government websites.
After the attack in Australia, politicians there are demanding answers, and top executives will soon be called to account there.
A professor laughed when Politiken asked whether Denmark is prepared to handle AI agents.

copy.headline: Denmark beat Wales 2-0 for their first Nations League points

standard.text: Denmark beat Wales 2-0 in Parken on Sunday evening with a goal from Gustav Isaksen and a Welsh own goal, both in the second half. The win gave Denmark their first three points in the Nations League group, after the defeat in Norway.
Coach Brian Riemer is still under pressure, Berlingske writes, but much less than the day before.
Several Danish players came close to top marks from DR's football commentators Andreas Kraul and Kenneth Møller Pedersen.

copy.headline: Thousands march in Madrid after an 87-year-old is evicted from her home of 70 years

standard.text: Thousands marched in Madrid on Saturday for stronger tenant protection, after 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted on Wednesday from her home of more than 70 years. Her new landlord wanted to raise the rent by 275 per cent to 2,650 euros a month, according to the tenants' union.
The authorities put the turnout at 25,000; the tenants' union says more than 300,000 came.

The government is expected to approve a package nicknamed the 'Maricarmen decree' at its next cabinet meeting, with automatic extension of leases and further limits on evictions. It lacks a majority in parliament, which rejected a similar package last year.
